questions.question: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis established the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Statistical Institute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, a legendary Indian statistician, founded the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** on **17th December 1931**.
 
• The institute was established in **Kolkata** (formerly Calcutta) and initially functioned from the **Statistical Laboratory** located in the **Presidency College**.
 
• The **Indian Statistical Institute** was recognized as an **Institute of National Importance** by the **Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959**, passed by the **Parliament of India**.
 
• Mahalanobis is widely celebrated as the **"Father of Indian Statistics"** for his immense contribution to the development of the field in the country.
 
• The establishment of **ISI** was a pivotal moment for **scientific research** in India, as it integrated **statistics** with various natural and social sciences. ***Hence, the correct option is Indian Statistical Institute.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahalanobis Distance**: One of his most significant scientific contributions is the **Mahalanobis Distance**, introduced in **1936**, which is a statistical measure used to find the distance between a point and a distribution.
 
• **National Statistics Day**: In recognition of his contributions to **economic planning** and **statistical development**, the **Government of India** celebrates his birth anniversary, **June 29**, as **National Statistics Day** every year.
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**: Mahalanobis was a key member of the **Planning Commission** and formulated the **Mahalanobis Model** for the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, which emphasized **rapid industrialization** and the growth of **heavy industries**.
 
• **National Sample Survey (NSS)**: He was instrumental in establishing the **National Sample Survey** in **1950** and the **Central Statistical Organisation (CSO)** to provide a comprehensive database for the Indian economy.
 
• **Honours**: For his distinguished service, he was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1968** and was a fellow of several international organizations, including the **Royal Society of London**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**: It is India's central bank established on **April 1, 1935**, following the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**. It was not founded by Mahalanobis but was established based on the **Hilton Young Commission** recommendations.
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI)**: It was created on **July 1, 1955**, after the nationalization of the **Imperial Bank of India**. It is the largest public sector bank in the country.
 
• **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**: While Mahalanobis founded the **NSS** in **1950**, the **NSSO** was a government organization under **MoSPI**. In **2019**, the **NSSO** was merged with the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)** to form the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**.
 
• **Sankhya**: Mahalanobis also started **Sankhya: The Indian Journal of Statistics** in **1933**, which remains a prestigious publication in the field of statistics worldwide.

questions.question: Which one of the following chronological order (from first to last) regarding the rule of early Turkish rulers is correct?

options.text: Qutbuddin Aybak, Shamsuddin Iltutmish, Ghiyasuddin Balban
Ghiyasuddin Balban, Qutbuddin Aybak, Shamsuddin Iltutmish
Shamsuddin Iltutmish, Ghiyasuddin Balban, Qutbuddin Aybak
Ghiyasuddin Balban, Shamsuddin Iltutmish, Qutbuddin Aybak

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutbuddin Aybak, Shamsuddin Iltutmish, Ghiyasuddin Balban**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Sultanate** was ruled by five successive dynasties, the first of which was the **Mamluk Dynasty** (also known as the **Slave Dynasty**), established by **Turkish rulers**.
 
• **Qutbuddin Aybak** was the first ruler of the **Mamluk Dynasty**, reigning from **1206 to 1210 AD**. He was a former slave of **Muhammad Ghori** and laid the foundation of the **Delhi Sultanate** after Ghori's death.
 
• **Shamsuddin Iltutmish** succeeded to the throne after a brief interval following Aybak's death, ruling from **1211 to 1236 AD**. He is often regarded as the **real consolidator** of the Turkish rule in India and shifted the capital from **Lahore** to **Delhi**.
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban** was another prominent Turkish ruler who ascended the throne much later, reigning from **1266 to 1287 AD**. He served as the **Naib** (regent) to Sultan **Nasiruddin Mahmud** before becoming the Sultan himself.
 
• The correct chronological order starts with the founder **Qutbuddin Aybak (1206)**, followed by the consolidator **Shamsuddin Iltutmish (1211)**, and finally the powerful administrator **Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266)**. ***Hence, the sequence in option 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Qutbuddin Aybak (Reign: 1206–1210):**

 
 
• Known as **Lakh Baksh** (giver of lakhs) for his generosity.
 
• He started the construction of the **Qutub Minar** in **Delhi**, dedicated to the Sufi saint **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.
 
• He died in **1210** while playing **Chaugan** (an early form of polo) in **Lahore**.
 
 
 
• **Shamsuddin Iltutmish (Reign: 1211–1236):**
 
 
• He introduced the **Iqta system** of land distribution and civil administration.
 
• He issued the first standard Arabic coinage of the Sultanate: the **Silver Tanka** and the **Copper Jital**.
 
• He organized a group of forty powerful Turkish nobles known as **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (The Forty).
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban (Reign: 1266–1287):**
 
 
• He adopted the policy of **Blood and Iron** to suppress internal revolts and external Mongol threats.
 
• He introduced the Persian customs of **Sijdah** (prostration) and **Paibos** (kissing the Sultan's feet) in his court.
 
• He broke the power of the **Chahalgani** nobles to centralize authority and established a centralized spy system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Mamluk** refers to an **Arabic** word for "owned," signifying that these rulers were originally **military slaves** who rose to sovereign status.
 
• Between **Iltutmish** and **Balban**, other notable rulers included **Razia Sultan** (the first female Muslim ruler of India, **1236–1240**) and **Nasiruddin Mahmud** (**1246–1266**).
 
• The **Slave Dynasty** came to an end in **1290 AD** when **Jalaluddin Khalji** overthrew the last Mamluk ruler, **Kayumars**, to establish the **Khalji Dynasty**.
 
• The primary sources for this period include **Tabaqat-i-Nasiri** by **Minhaj-us-Siraj** and later accounts by **Ziauddin Barani**.

questions.question: Which of the following five year plan had the theme "Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eleventh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eleventh Five-Year Plan** of India spanned the period from **2007 to 2012**.
 
• The central theme and objective of this plan was **"Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth"**. This was a significant shift in planning strategy, moving from mere economic expansion to ensuring that the benefits of growth reached all sections of society.
 
• It was prepared under the chairmanship of **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, who was the **Prime Minister** at that time, and the core document was drafted by the **Planning Commission**.
 
• The plan aimed to increase the **GDP growth rate** to **9%** and specifically targeted a **4% growth rate** in the **agricultural sector** to sustain rural livelihoods.
 
• Key goals included the creation of **70 million new work opportunities**, reduction of **infant mortality rate (IMR)** to **28** per 1000 live births, and ensuring **clean drinking water** for all by **2009**.
 
• It placed heavy emphasis on the **social sector**, particularly **education** and **health**, often being referred to as the "Education Plan" due to the high allocation of funds toward **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan** and higher education.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Eleventh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):**

 
 
• This plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** with a primary focus on the **agricultural sector**, including investments in dams and **irrigation**.
 
• The **Bhakra Nangal Dam** and **Hirakud Dam** projects were initiated during this period to address the food shortage after **Independence** and **Partition**.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1978):**
 
 
• The top priority of this plan was **Garibi Hatao** (poverty removal) and the **attainment of self-reliance**.
 
• The draft of this plan was prepared and launched by **D.P. Dhar**. However, it was terminated one year early in **1978** by the newly elected **Janata Party** government, which introduced the **Rolling Plan**.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985–1990):**
 
 
• This plan focused on the theme of **"Food, Work, and Productivity"** under the leadership of **Rajiv Gandhi**.
 
• It emphasized the growth of **food grain production**, increasing **employment opportunities**, and raising **productivity** through the integration of **technology** and **social justice**.
 
 
 
• **Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017):**
 
 
• The **Twelfth Plan** was the final Five-Year Plan of India before the **Planning Commission** was replaced by **NITI Aayog**.
 
• Its theme was **"Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth"**, adding the crucial component of **environmental sustainability** to the previous plan's objective.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Planning:** Economic planning in India started in **1950** with the setting up of the **Planning Commission**. The **National Development Council (NDC)** was responsible for the final approval of these plans.
 
• **Major Shift:** In **January 2015**, the **NDA government** dissolved the Planning Commission and established **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) to serve as a **think-tank** for the government, promoting **cooperative federalism**.
 
• **Key Terms:** **Inclusive growth** refers to a growth process that yields broad-based benefits and ensures equality of opportunity for all, specifically focusing on the **marginalized sections** like **SC, ST, OBCs, and Minorities**.

questions.question: Sri Lanka is separated from India by the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palk strait**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Palk Strait** is a narrow inlet of the **Indian Ocean** located between the southeastern coast of **India** and the northern coast of **Sri Lanka**.
 
• It connects the **Bay of Bengal** in the northeast with the **Palk Bay** in the southwest, which further connects to the **Gulf of Mannar**.
 
• The strait is named after **Robert Palk**, who served as the **Governor of Madras Presidency** during the **British Raj** period between **1755 and 1763**.
 
• It is characterized by a chain of low islands and reef shoals known as **Adam's Bridge** (also popularly called **Ram Setu**), which stretches across the strait from **Dhanushkodi** on **Pamban Island** in **Tamil Nadu** to **Mannar Island** in **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The width of the **Palk Strait** ranges from approximately **64 to 137 kilometers**, and it is relatively **shallow**, making it difficult for large ships to pass through without specific channels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Malacca Strait**:

 
 
• It is a narrow stretch of water located between the **Malay Peninsula** and the Indonesian island of **Sumatra**.
 
• It serves as the main shipping channel between the **Indian Ocean** and the **Pacific Ocean**, connecting major economies like **India, China, Japan, and South Korea**.
 
• It is one of the busiest and most **strategically important** maritime **chokepoints** in the world for **global trade**.
 
 
 
• **Hormuz Strait**:
 
 
• Located between the **Persian Gulf** and the **Gulf of Oman**, it separates **Iran** from the **Arabian Peninsula** (specifically **Oman** and the **UAE**).
 
• It is the world's most important **oil transit chokepoint**, as a significant portion of the world's **petroleum** consumption passes through this narrow waterway daily.
 
 
 
• **Cook Strait**:
 
 
• This strait separates the **North Island** and **South Island** of **New Zealand**.
 
• It connects the **Tasman Sea** on the northwest with the **South Pacific Ocean** on the southeast.
 
• It is named after **James Cook**, the first European commander to sail through it in **1770**, and it is known for its strong **tidal currents** and unpredictable weather.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Sethusamudram Shipping Canal Project** is a proposed project by the **Government of India** to create a shipping route in the **shallow waters** of the **Palk Strait** to reduce travel time for ships.
 
• Several rivers of **Tamil Nadu**, including the **Vaigai River**, drain into the **Palk Strait**.
 
• The region is rich in **biodiversity**, particularly the nearby **Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park**, which is a designated **Biosphere Reserve** containing numerous species of **coral reefs**, **dugongs**, and **sea turtles**.

questions.question: The land mass of India has an area of ____ million square km.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **land mass** of **India** has an **area** of approximately **3.28 million square km**, which is officially recorded as **3,287,263 square kilometres**.
 
• India's total area accounts for about **2.4 percent** of the total **geographical area** of the **world**.
 
• In terms of **land area**, **India** is the **seventh largest country** in the world, preceded by **Russia**, **Canada**, **USA**, **China**, **Brazil**, and **Australia**.
 
• The **north-south extent** of the country from **Kashmir** to **Kanniyakumari** is about **3,214 km**.
 
• The **east-west width** from **Arunachal Pradesh** to **Gujarat** (specifically **Kuchchh**) is approximately **2,933 km**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Boundaries**:

 
 
• India has a **land boundary** of about **15,200 km**.
 
• The total length of the **coastline** of the mainland, including the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** and **Lakshadweep**, is **7,516.6 km**.
 
• India is bounded by the **young fold mountains** (the **Himalayas**) in the **northwest**, **north**, and **northeast**.
 
 
 
• **International Borders**:
 
 
• India shares its land borders with **seven countries**: **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan** in the northwest; **China**, **Nepal**, and **Bhutan** in the north; and **Myanmar** and **Bangladesh** in the east.
 
• The longest border is shared with **Bangladesh**, measuring approximately **4,096.7 km**.
 
 
 
• **Location and Coordinates**:
 
 
• The **mainland** of India extends between **latitudes 8°4'N and 37°6'N** and **longitudes 68°7'E and 97°25'E**.
 
• The **Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N)** passes through **eight Indian states**: **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Standard Time**: The **Standard Meridian of India** is **82°30'E**, passing through **Mirzapur** in **Uttar Pradesh**. The time along this meridian is taken as the **Standard Time (IST)** for the whole country.
 
• **Southernmost Point**: While the southernmost point of the **mainland** is **Kanniyakumari**, the southernmost point of the **Indian Union** was **Indira Point** (located in the **Great Nicobar Island**), which got submerged under the sea water in **2004** during the **Tsunami**.
 
• **Administrative Structure**: For administrative purposes, the country is divided into **28 States** and **8 Union Territories** as of the latest reorganization following the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• **Strategic Position**: The **Indian landmass** has a **central location** between **East** and **West Asia**, and the **trans-Indian Ocean routes** connect the countries of **Europe** in the West and the countries of **East Asia**.

questions.question: The ______ feet high iron pillar at Mehrauli in Delhi too speaks volumes of the iron technology prevailing in the Gupta period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iron Pillar of Delhi** stands at a total height of **7.21 meters**, which is approximately **23 feet**, with a portion of about **1.12 meters** currently below the ground level.
 
• Located at the **Qutub Complex** in **Mehrauli**, Delhi, this historical monument is globally renowned for its exceptional **rust-resistant** properties, surviving over **1,600 years** without significant corrosion.
 
• It was erected during the reign of **Chandragupta II** (reigned c. 375–415 CE) of the **Gupta Dynasty**, a period often referred to as the **Golden Age of India**.
 
• The pillar weighs more than **6,000 kilograms** (6 tonnes) and was manufactured using **forge-welding** techniques, indicating the sophisticated **metallurgical skills** of ancient Indian blacksmiths.
 
• An **inscription** in the **Brahmi script** and **Sanskrit language** on the pillar mentions a king named **Chandra**, who is identified by most historians as **Chandragupta Vikramaditya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metallurgical Composition:**

 
 
• Scientific analysis shows that the pillar contains a high amount of **phosphorus** (0.11%) and lacks **sulfur** and **magnesium**.
 
• The corrosion resistance is attributed to the formation of a protective layer called **misawite** (crystalline iron oxyhydroxide) on the surface, which is catalyzed by the high phosphorus content and the specific **atmospheric conditions** of Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The pillar was originally a **Vishnudhvaja** (Standard of Lord Vishnu) and was likely situated at **Udayagiri** or **Vishnupadagiri** before being moved to its current location in Delhi by **Anangpal Tomar** in the **11th century**.
 
• It serves as primary evidence of the progress in **science and technology** during the **Gupta Era**, complementing other advancements like the **decimal system** and **astronomy**.

questions.question: Which of the following article of Indian Constitution deals with Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List if a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 250**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 250** of the **Indian Constitution** confers power upon the **Parliament** to make laws for the entire territory of India or any part of it regarding any matter listed in the **State List** (List II) during a **Proclamation of Emergency**.
 
• This provision is activated when a **National Emergency** is declared by the President under **Article 352** on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• Laws enacted by the Parliament under **Article 250** remain valid only while the proclamation is in force and for a period of **six months** after the emergency has ceased to operate.
 
• The primary objective of this article is to maintain **national integrity** and ensure **legislative coordination** during times of crisis, temporarily shifting the federal balance toward a **unitary structure**.
 
• Even while **Article 250** is in operation, the **State Legislature** is not prohibited from making laws on the same subject, but in case of a conflict, the **Parliamentary law** prevails as per **Article 251**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 282**:

 
 
• Relates to **discretionary grants** that can be made by the **Union** or a **State** for any **public purpose**, regardless of whether it falls within their respective legislative domains.
 
 
 
• **Article 263**:
 
 
• Deals with the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** by the **President** to facilitate **coordination**, **inquiry**, and **advice** on disputes between States or the Union.
 
 
 
• **Article 173**:
 
 
• Specifies the **qualifications** for membership in a **State Legislature**, including **citizenship of India** and minimum age limits (**25 years** for the Legislative Assembly and **30 years** for the Legislative Council).

questions.question: ‘Gaarudi Gombe’, performed during major festivals, is a folk dance of which Indian state/Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaarudi Gombe** is a unique and vibrant folk dance native to the state of **Karnataka**, specifically popular in the **Old Mysore** region.
 
• The name literally translates to **Magical Doll** in the **Kannada** language, referring to the giant puppets used in the performance.
 
• The puppets are constructed using a **bamboo wicker frame**, standing approximately 10 to 12 feet tall and weighing between 30 to 40 kilograms.
 
• Performers carry these massive structures on their shoulders, balancing them while executing rhythmic dance steps to the beats of the **Tamate** (drum).
 
• The face of the doll is typically crafted from **papier-mache** and painted to represent various mythological characters, folk heroes, or deities.
 
• This art form is a major attraction during the **Mysuru Dasara** procession and is frequently performed during **Ugadhi** and village fairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Bengal**:

 
 
• Known for **Chhau**, a masked tribal dance that depicts episodes from epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• **Gambhira** and **Brita** are other significant traditional dances of this region.
 
 
 
• **Tripura**:
 
 
• Home to **Hojagiri**, a dance of the **Reang** clan where women balance pitchers and lamps while performing intricate footwork.
 
• Other folk forms include **Garia** and **Lebang Boomani**.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**:
 
 
• **Rouf** is a famous folk dance performed by women during **Eid** and spring seasons.
 
• **Bhand Pather** is a traditional folk theatre involving dance and satire.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka (Other Arts)**:
 
 
• **Dollu Kunitha**: A high-energy drum dance associated with the **Kuruba** community.
 
• **Yakshagana**: A classical theater form combining dance, music, and elaborate costumes.

questions.question: Meristematic tissue is classified into how many types?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** are a group of young cells that consist of actively dividing cells and are responsible for the **growth and development** of the plant.
 
• Based on their **location or position** in the plant body, these tissues are classified into **three distinct types**: **Apical Meristem**, **Intercalary Meristem**, and **Lateral Meristem**.
 
• **Apical Meristem**: It is located at the **growing tips of stems and roots** (the apices). Its primary function is to increase the **vertical length** of the plant, known as **primary growth**.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem**: These are located at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (e.g., in grasses). They facilitate the **lengthening of the internode** and help in the regrowth of parts removed by grazing animals.
 
• **Lateral Meristem**: Situated on the **lateral sides** of the plant body, parallel to the longitudinal axis. It is responsible for **secondary growth**, which increases the **girth or thickness** of the stem and root. Examples include **Vascular Cambium** and **Cork Cambium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Meristematic Cells**:

 
 
• The cells are **immature**, small, and generally **isodiametric** (spherical, oval, or polygonal) in shape.
 
• They possess **thin cell walls** made primarily of **cellulose** and lack **intercellular spaces**.
 
• Each cell contains a **dense cytoplasm**, a **large and prominent nucleus**, and typically lacks **vacuoles** due to high metabolic activity.
 
• These tissues remain in a state of **continuous division** until they differentiate into **permanent tissues**.
 
 
 
• **Other Classifications**:
 
 
• **Based on Origin**: Meristems can also be grouped into **Promeristem**, **Primary Meristem**, and **Secondary Meristem** depending on their developmental stage in the plant life cycle.

questions.question: In which Indian state/UT is the 'Three Kings Feast' festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Three Kings Feast**, popularly known as **Festa dos Reis** or the **Feast of Epiphany**, is a significant religious and cultural festival celebrated in the Indian state of **Goa**.
 
• It is observed annually on **January 6th**, marking the conclusion of the Christmas season and the manifestation of **Jesus Christ** to the Gentiles.

questions.question: The recoil experienced when firing a bullet from a gun is an example of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's third law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion** states that for every **action**, there is always an **equal and opposite reaction**. These two forces act on different bodies and never cancel each other out.
 
• When a **bullet** is fired from a **gun**, the gun exerts a forward force on the bullet to accelerate it. This is the **action force**.
 
• According to the law, the bullet simultaneously exerts an equal amount of force on the gun in the backward direction. This is the **reaction force**.
 
• The backward motion of the gun resulting from this reaction force is specifically known as the **recoil** of the gun.
 
• This interaction also illustrates the **Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum**. Since the initial total momentum of the system (gun + bullet) is zero, the final total momentum must also be zero, meaning the forward momentum of the bullet is balanced by the backward momentum of the gun.
 
• The **recoil velocity** of the gun is significantly lower than the velocity of the bullet because the **mass** of the gun is much larger than the mass of the bullet, keeping the product of mass and velocity (momentum) equal for both.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**:

 
 
• Often called the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an **external applied force**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**:
 
 
• This law provides a quantitative definition of force, stating that the rate of change of **momentum** of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** applied. It is mathematically expressed as **F = ma** (Force equals mass times acceleration).
 
 
 
• **Newton's Law of Gravitation**:
 
 
• A universal law stating that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points. The force is proportional to the product of the **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between them.

• The term **Shiv** represents the welfare of humanity, while **Shakti** represents the capability and strength of **women scientists** who contributed significantly to the mission.
 
• The site is located at approximately **69.37°S latitude** and **32.35°E longitude** on the **Moon**, situated between the **Manzinus C** and **Simpelius N** craters.

• The mission consisted of a **Propulsion Module**, the **Vikram Lander**, and the **Pragyan Rover**.
 
 
 
• **Tiranga Point:**
 
 
• This is the name designated for the site where the **Chandrayaan-2** lander crashed on the **Moon** in **2019**.
 
• It serves as a reminder that no failure is permanent and symbolizes **India's** resilience in **space exploration**.

• **Scientific Importance:** The **lunar south pole** is of great interest to the **global scientific community** because of the presence of **water ice** in permanently shadowed craters, which could support future **human missions**.
 
• **ISRO's Achievement:** With this mission, **India** became the **fourth country** in the world to achieve a soft landing on the **Moon**, joining the **United States**, the **Soviet Union**, and **China**.
 
• **Rover Findings:** The **Pragyan Rover** confirmed the presence of **Sulfur (S)** on the lunar surface near the south pole and detected other elements like **Aluminum, Calcium, Iron, and Titanium**.

questions.question: Which space agency's Hubble Space Telescope captured a cosmic ‘bullseye galaxy’ with nine rings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NASA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hubble Space Telescope (HST)**, which captured the stunning image of a **"bullseye galaxy"** featuring intricate rings of dust, is a project of international cooperation between **NASA** (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) and **ESA** (European Space Agency).
 
• The "bullseye" appearance specifically refers to galaxies like **NGC 4753**, where Hubble’s high-resolution imaging revealed **concentric dust rings** wrapping around the galactic core, likely formed by a past **galactic merger** event.
 
• Launched on **April 24, 1990**, aboard the **Space Shuttle Discovery**, Hubble has been operational for over **three decades**, providing unprecedented views of the universe from its position in **Low Earth Orbit**.
 
• The telescope is managed by **NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center** in Greenbelt, Maryland, while the **Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI)** conducts the science operations.
 
• Hubble's ability to observe in **ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared** light allows it to capture details such as the **nine rings** of dust or gas that are often invisible to ground-based telescopes due to atmospheric distortion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration):**

 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is the **United States** government agency responsible for the civilian space program and aeronautics research.
 
• Apart from Hubble, NASA operates the **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)** and the **Chandra X-ray Observatory**.
 
 
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation):**
 
 
• Headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it is India’s national space agency.
 
• In **2015**, ISRO launched **AstroSat**, which is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, though it is smaller in scale than Hubble.
 
 
 
• **JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency):**
 
 
• Formed in **2003**, it is **Japan's** national aerospace agency.
 
• JAXA is known for pioneering missions like **Hayabusa2**, which returned samples from the asteroid **Ryugu**.
 
 
 
• **CNES (Centre National d'Études Spatiales):**
 
 
• The **French** government space agency, founded in **1961**.
 
• It plays a key role in the **European Space Agency (ESA)** and often collaborates with NASA on Earth observation and Mars exploration missions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Hubble's Legacy:** It helped determine the **age of the universe** (approx. **13.8 billion years**) and confirmed the existence of **supermassive black holes** at the centers of galaxies.
 
• **Maintenance:** Unlike many other telescopes, Hubble was designed to be serviced in space by **astronauts**, with **five servicing missions** conducted between **1993 and 2009** to upgrade its cameras and sensors.

questions.question: The principal mineral-bearing belts in __________ are Vidarbha area and Konkan area.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distribution of minerals in **Maharashtra** is highly uneven, with the majority of deposits concentrated in the **Vidarbha** region in the east and the **Konkan** region in the west.
 
• While the **Deccan Trap** (basaltic lava) covers nearly **80%** to **85%** of the state's total area, these rocks are generally devoid of major mineral deposits, except for building stones and some bauxite.
 
• The **Vidarbha** area, particularly districts like **Nagpur**, **Bhandara**, **Chandrapur**, **Gadchiroli**, and **Yavatmal**, is the powerhouse of the state's mineral wealth, containing significant reserves of **Coal**, **Manganese**, and **Iron Ore**.
 
• The **Konkan** area and parts of **South Maharashtra** (like **Kolhapur**, **Ratnagiri**, and **Sindhudurg**) are rich in **Bauxite** and **Iron Ore** due to the presence of **Laterite** soil and specific geological formations.
 
• Approximately **12.33%** of the total geographical area of **Maharashtra** is considered "mineral-bearing," providing essential raw materials for industries like **Steel**, **Cement**, and **Aluminium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Coal Resources:**

 
 
• **Coal** is the most important mineral found in the **Vidarbha** region. It is found in the **Gondwana** rock systems along the **Wardha** and **Wainganga** river basins.
 
• Major coal-producing areas include **Chandrapur**, **Ballarpur**, **Warora**, **Umred**, and **Kamptee**. These reserves feed several **Thermal Power Plants** in the state.
 
 
 
• **Manganese and Iron Ore:**
 
 
• **Maharashtra** is one of the leading producers of **Manganese** in **India**. High-grade deposits are found in the **Nagpur** and **Bhandara** districts.
 
• **Iron Ore** is found in the **Surajgarh** and **Deulgaon** areas of **Gadchiroli** (eastern belt) and in the **Redi** area of **Sindhudurg** district (western belt). The **Redi** port is crucial for the export of iron ore to countries like **Japan** and **China**.
 
 
 
• **Bauxite and Limestone:**
 
 
• **Bauxite**, the primary ore for **Aluminium**, is found in the laterite caps of the **Sahyadri** ranges. Key locations include **Kolhapur** (Radhanagari, Shahuwadi), **Ratnagiri**, and **Raigad**.
 
• **Limestone** is vital for the **Cement** industry. Massive deposits are found in **Yavatmal** and **Chandrapur** districts, making this region a hub for cement manufacturing units.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Directorate of Geology and Mining (DGM):** This department, headquartered in **Nagpur**, was established in **1948**. It is responsible for the systematic exploration, assessment, and administration of mineral resources in **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The mining sector contributes significantly to the state's **Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP)**. Districts like **Chandrapur** are often referred to as the "Black Gold City" due to the abundance of coal.
 
• **Other Minerals:** Besides the major ones, the state also possesses deposits of **Chromite** (Bhandara, Sindhudurg), **Kyanite** and **Sillimanite** (Bhandara), and **Dolomite** (Yavatmal, Nagpur).
 
• **Crude Oil:** While not part of the Vidarbha or Konkan terrestrial belts, the **Mumbai High** (offshore Konkan coast) is India's largest **Oil** and **Natural Gas** field, operated by **ONGC**.

questions.question: In which year was the National Statistical Commission was constituted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2006**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Statistical Commission (NSC)** of **India** was formally constituted on **12th July 2006**.
 
• The establishment of this body was based on the recommendations of the **Rangarajan Commission**, headed by **Dr. C. Rangarajan**, which submitted its report in **2001** to address the gaps in the Indian statistical system.
 
• The government issued a notification for the setting up of the commission on **1st June 2005**, leading to its actual constitution in the subsequent year.
 
• The **NSC** was designed to serve as an **autonomous body** responsible for evolving policies, priorities, and standards in statistical matters to ensure the credibility of official data.
 
• The first Chairman of the **National Statistical Commission** was the renowned economist **Professor Suresh Tendulkar**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 2006**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Organizational Structure**:

 
 
• The commission consists of a part-time **Chairperson**, four part-time **Members**, and an ex-officio member.
 
• The **CEO** of **NITI Aayog** (formerly the Planning Commission) serves as the ex-officio member.
 
• The **Chief Statistician of India (CSI)**, who is also the Secretary to the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, acts as the Secretary to the Commission.
 
 
 
• **Mandate and Functions**:
 
 
• The primary function of the **NSC** is to reduce the burden on data providers and improve the efficiency of the statistical system.
 
• It helps in standardizing **statistical concepts**, **definitions**, and **methodologies** used by various central and state government agencies.
 
• It exercises oversight over the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** and the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)**.
 
 
 
• **MoSPI**:
 
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation** is the nodal agency for the planned development of the statistical system in the country.
 
• It ensures the timely release of key economic indicators like **GDP**, **CPI**, and **IIP**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Statistics Day**:

 
 
• In **India**, **June 29th** is celebrated as **National Statistics Day** every year.
 
• This day marks the birth anniversary of **Professor Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, often referred to as the father of modern statistics in **India**, in recognition of his invaluable contribution in establishing the **National Statistical System**.
 
 
 
• **Merger of CSO and NSSO**:
 
 
• In **May 2019**, the **Government of India** approved the merger of the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)** and the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** to create a unified **National Statistical Office (NSO)**.
 
• This restructuring was aimed at streamlining the data collection and processing activities under the umbrella of **MoSPI**.
 
 
 
• **Rangarajan Commission Report**:
 
 
• The commission was set up in **January 2000** and submitted its findings in **August 2001**. It highlighted that the lack of coordination and the absence of a legislative framework were major hurdles in the statistical system, leading to the creation of the **NSC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **wicket-keeper** is a specialist **fielder** in the sport of **cricket** who stands behind the **stumps** at the striker's end of the pitch.
 
• Under the **Laws of Cricket**, specifically **Law 27**, the **wicket-keeper** is the only member of the fielding side permitted to wear **gloves** and external **leg guards** (pads).
 
• The primary responsibility of the **wicket-keeper** is to stop deliveries that pass the **batter** and to attempt to dismiss the **batter** through a **catch** or a **stumping**.
 
• A **stumping** occurs when the **wicket-keeper** puts down the **wicket** while the **batter** is out of their ground (crease) and not attempting a run.
 
• The **wicket-keeper** plays a crucial role in the fielding side's strategy, often acting as a "general" who provides feedback to the **bowler** and helps the captain with **field placements** due to their unique vantage point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Batter**:

 
 
• A **batter** is the player currently at the **crease** whose objective is to score **runs** and prevent the ball from hitting the **stumps**.
 
• They use a **bat** made of **willow wood** and wear protective gear including a **helmet**, **gloves**, **pads**, and **arm guards**.
 
 
 
• **Bowler**:
 
 
• The **bowler** is the player who delivers the ball to the **batter**. The act of delivering the ball is called **bowling**.
 
• **Bowlers** are generally categorized into **fast bowlers** (who rely on speed) and **spin bowlers** (who use finger or wrist action to change the ball's trajectory).
 
 
 
• **Umpire**:
 
 
• The **umpire** is an official who has the authority to make decisions about events on the **cricket field** according to the **Laws of Cricket**.
 
• There are usually **two on-field umpires** and a **third umpire** (television umpire) who assists with close calls using technology like **ball-tracking** and **ultra-edge**.
 
 
 
• **Equipment and Rules**:
 
 
• The **wicket-keeper's gloves** must have **webbing** between the thumb and the index finger, but only to a specified **size** and **standard** regulated by the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)**.
 
• Modern **wicket-keepers** almost always wear a **helmet** when standing close to the **stumps** for a **spinner** to protect against fast-moving balls or accidental hits from the **bat**.
 
• Famous **wicket-keepers** in the history of the game include **MS Dhoni** from **India**, **Adam Gilchrist** from **Australia**, and **Kumar Sangakkara** from **Sri Lanka**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **wicket-keeper** must remain wholly behind the **stumps** until the ball has been touched by the **batter** or has passed the **wicket**.
 
• If the **wicket-keeper** moves significantly before the ball is delivered, it can be called a **dead ball** or lead to penalties.
 
• In **Test cricket**, the **wicket-keeper** is often required to stay focused for up to **90 overs** a day, making it one of the most physically and mentally demanding positions in the sport.

• The primary objective of the game is to shoot a **ball** through a raised hoop, known as the **basket** or **rim**, which is mounted at a height of **10 feet** (**3.048 meters**) to a **backboard** at each end of the court.
 
• The sport was invented in **December 1891** by **Dr. James Naismith**, a Canadian physical education instructor, in **Springfield, Massachusetts**, as a way to keep his students active indoors during the winter.
 
• The international governing body for the sport is **FIBA** (**International Basketball Federation**), which was founded in **1932**.
 
• A standard professional basketball court measures **28 by 15 meters** under **FIBA** rules and **94 by 50 feet** in the **NBA** (**National Basketball Association**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Dribbling**: The act of bouncing the ball continuously with one hand while walking or running.
 
• **Rebound**: Gaining possession of the ball after a missed **field goal** or **free throw**.
 
• **Layup**: A **two-point** shot attempt made by leaping from below, laying the ball up near the basket, and using one hand to bounce it off the backboard and into the basket.
 
• **Three-pointer**: A field goal made from beyond the **three-point line**, a designated arc surrounding the basket.
 
 
 
• **Gameplay Duration:**
 
 
• In the **NBA**, a game consists of **four quarters** of **12 minutes** each.
 
• Under **FIBA** regulations, the game consists of **four quarters** of **10 minutes** each.
 
 
 
• **Major Organizations:**
 
 
• The **NBA**, based in **North America**, is widely considered the premier professional basketball league in the world in terms of popularity, salaries, and level of competition.
 
• **Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA)** is the equivalent professional league for women in the **United States**.

• **Player Positions:**

 
 
• **Point Guard (PG)**: Usually the team's best ball handler and passer, responsible for directing the offense.
 
• **Shooting Guard (SG)**: Typically the team's best outside shooter.
 
• **Small Forward (SF)**: Often a versatile player responsible for scoring and rebounding.
 
• **Power Forward (PF)**: Plays offensively with their back to the basket and focuses on defense and rebounding.
 
• **Center (C)**: Usually the tallest player, positioned near the basket to block shots and secure rebounds.
 
 
 
• **Violations and Fouls:**
 
 
• **Traveling**: Taking more than two steps without dribbling the ball.
 
• **Double Dribble**: Dribbling the ball with two hands at the same time or stopping the dribble and then starting again.
 
• **Personal Foul**: Illegal physical contact with an opponent.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Sushir Vadya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bargu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sushir Vadya**, also known as **Aerophones**, are musical instruments where sound is produced by the vibration of air, typically blown through a tube or a reed.
 
• **Bargu** is a traditional wind instrument primarily found in the state of **Rajasthan**, India. It is a long, curved trumpet or horn made of **brass** or **copper**.
 
• This instrument is widely associated with the **Bhil tribe** of **Rajasthan** and **Madhya Pradesh**. It is commonly played during community gatherings, **festivals**, and traditional ceremonies like **weddings**.
 
• The **Bargu** is frequently used to accompany the **Gair dance**, a famous tribal dance of the **Bhils**, providing a deep, resonant sound that signals the beginning of performances or religious processions.
 
• Historically, such horns were also used as signaling devices to warn villagers of approaching **threats** or to announce the arrival of important **dignitaries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Musical Instruments:**

 
 
• In the ancient text **Natya Shastra**, written by **Bharat Muni** between **200 BC and 200 AD**, Indian musical instruments are classified into **four** main categories.
 
• **Tata Vadya (Chordophones):** These are stringed instruments. Examples include the **Veena**, **Sitar**, **Sarangi**, and the **Pena** (a traditional bowed instrument of **Manipur**).
 
• **Sushir Vadya (Aerophones):** These are wind instruments. Examples include the **Bansuri** (flute), **Shehnai**, **Shankh** (conch), **Pungi**, and **Bargu**.
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya (Membranophones):** These are percussion instruments with a stretched skin or membrane. Examples include the **Tabla**, **Dholak**, **Mridangam**, and **Nagada**.
 
• **Ghana Vadya (Idiophones):** These are solid instruments made of metal or wood that do not require tuning. Examples include **Manjira**, **Jhanj**, **Karthal**, and **Hath ghanti** (hand bell).
 
 
 
• **Regional Wind Instruments:**
 
 
• **Mashak:** A type of **bagpipe** found in **Rajasthan** and **Uttarakhand**, often made from **goat skin**.
 
• **Algoza:** A double flute popular in **Punjab** and **Rajasthan** folk music, played simultaneously by the musician.
 
• **Karna:** A straight, long **brass** trumpet used in temple processions and royal announcements in **North India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Pena** is a **Tata Vadya** (string instrument) and is the oldest musical instrument of the **Meitei** people of **Manipur**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Hath ghanti** belongs to the **Ghana Vadya** category as it is a solid metal instrument that produces sound through the vibration of its own body. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Bargu** is specifically characterized as a **Sushir Vadya** because it requires the **player's breath** to resonate air within its metal body to produce sound. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bargu.***
 
• **Sushir Vadya** are often classified into two types: those where the air is blown through a **natural hole** (like a flute) and those using a **mechanical reed** (like the **Shehnai**).

questions.question: Whom did Mahatma Gandhi regard as his mentor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** and a renowned social reformer who **Mahatma Gandhi** regarded as his **political mentor**.
 
• After **Mahatma Gandhi** returned to **India** from **South Africa** in **January 1915**, he sought guidance from **Gokhale**, who advised him to travel across the **Indian subcontinent** for **one year** to understand the ground realities of the people before taking any political stance.
 
• **Gandhi** expressed his deep respect and intellectual debt to **Gokhale** in his book titled **"Gokhale, My Political Guru"**, published in **1955**.
 
• **Gokhale** was a leading figure of the **Moderate** faction of the **Congress**, advocating for **constitutional means**, **dialogue**, and **reforms** rather than radical or violent methods to achieve **Swaraj**.
 
• In **1905**, **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** founded the **Servants of India Society** in **Pune**, **Maharashtra**, with the aim of training Indians to devote their lives to the cause of the nation through social and humanitarian work.
 
• He also served as the **President** of the **Banaras Session** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1905**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:**

 
 
• Known as **"Punjab Kesari"** (the Lion of Punjab), he was a prominent leader of the **Extremist** wing of the **Congress** (part of the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio).
 
• He played a crucial role in the **Swadeshi Movement** and founded the **Punjab National Bank** in **1894**.
 
• He died in **1928** after sustaining injuries during a **lathi charge** while protesting against the **Simon Commission**.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:**
 
 
• Known as the **"Grand Old Man of India"**, he was a co-founder of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its **President** three times (**1886, 1893, and 1906**).
 
• He was the first **Indian** to be elected as a **Member of Parliament (MP)** in the **British House of Commons**.
 
• He authored the famous book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"**, which introduced the **"Drain of Wealth"** theory, explaining how **Britain** was depleting **India's** resources.
 
 
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose:**
 
 
• A radical nationalist leader who twice served as the **President** of the **Congress** (**1938 and 1939**) before resigning due to ideological differences with **Gandhi**.
 
• He founded the **All India Forward Bloc** in **1939** and later led the **Indian National Army (INA)** or **Azad Hind Fauj** to fight against **British** rule.
 
• Interestingly, despite their differences, it was **Bose** who first addressed **Mahatma Gandhi** as the **"Father of the Nation"** in a radio address from **Singapore** in **1944**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Political Ideology:** **Gokhale** believed in **secularism** and **education** as the primary tools for national awakening. He was a member of the **Imperial Legislative Council** from **1902** until his death in **1915**.
 
• **Role in Reforms:** He was instrumental in the formulation of the **Morley-Minto Reforms** of **1909**, which increased **Indian** participation in the legislative process, although it also introduced **separate electorates**.
 
• **Mentorship:** Besides **Gandhi**, **Gokhale** also influenced several other leaders, including **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** in his early years, who aspired to become the **"Muslim Gokhale"** due to his ambassadorial role for **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
 
• **Journalism:** **Gokhale** was associated with the journal **"Sudharak"** (The Reformer) and contributed significantly to the **Sarvajanik Sabha** journal.
